requirements.requirement: node1 (VyOS, lan-a router) resolves app.internal to node3's lan-a address for hosts on lan-a
requirements.summary: VyOS config.boot committed with static-host-mapping app.internal -> 10.10.1.10 and dns forwarding listen-address 10.10.1.254/allow-from 10.10.1.0/24 (cmd-916a1ee0e0274d56). pdns-recursor confirmed active and listening on 10.10.1.254:53 (cmd-2551eac9e1724c82, global:after_executor:node1:listening-sockets). node3 resolved app.internal to 10.10.1.10 via getent and direct dig against 10.10.1.254 both pre- and post-restart (cmd-87679d9766974197, cmd-608d380ef9cc4a01, cmd-6ca3967646394ded, cmd-9d9cb407549348eb).

requirements.requirement: node2 (OPNsense, lan-b router) resolves app.internal to node4's lan-b address for hosts on lan-b
requirements.summary: OPNsense config.xml updated with unboundplus host override app.internal -> 10.10.2.10 and a firewall pass rule for the lan-b interface (cmd-342ce631ff044fd8, cmd-86028ea8b40b4c51 shows the persisted host entry). Unbound confirmed listening on *:53 after 'configctl unbound start' (cmd-2b98082a051840e2). node4 resolved app.internal to 10.10.2.10 via getent and direct query against 10.10.2.254, both before and after restart (cmd-a8e08dbbaab14d3d, cmd-796bda9305e440c0, cmd-e9cbaa63bf984a25, cmd-8660484f28094950).

requirements.requirement: Correct per-side split-horizon topology (lan-a vs lan-b addressing/adjacency) underlying the DNS split
requirements.summary: Topology discovered via STP bridge-id correlation matching node1 eth2 to node3 ens7 (lan-a, same bridge-id) and node2 vtnet2 to node4 ens7 (lan-b, same bridge-id), and node1 eth1 to node2 vtnet1 (transit) (cmd-406bd02874b0438b, cmd-d0ea35fbaab547bf). Static addressing applied consistently with this mapping and DNS resolves correctly on each side, confirming the mapping was correct.

requirements.requirement: Provider-wide node-restart evidence protocol executed on all managed nodes
requirements.summary: For all four nodes a pre-restart boot identity and healthy DNS state was captured (cmd-9fcfdfcf28174005, cmd-79c27e02e2d64baf, cmd-afa4ad81048148ab, cmd-107d255f42c64b10), a restart was issued and acknowledged (cmd-a3494b866f4343f2, cmd-816ad69d2c394538, cmd-035f2e5fd0e444b8, cmd-8f0b56f5816341c9), a distinct post-restart boot identity was confirmed (cmd-2f612d64203a48a0, cmd-36bbe048a6144148, cmd-2d132efffc694b6b, cmd-b2446c4037f4435f), and recovered interface/service/DNS state was verified (cmd-8e70762258974a8a, cmd-6ca3967646394ded, cmd-7f190b8ec922415f, cmd-e9cbaa63bf984a25, cmd-c51a2b75e2d74e83, cmd-9d9cb407549348eb, cmd-e129147e5ad04e09, cmd-8660484f28094950). The fixed after-executor boot-identity snapshots independently match the executor-reported post-restart boot ids for all four nodes.

overall_summary: Both material DNS-split requirements are satisfied with direct evidence: node1 (VyOS) resolves app.internal to node3's lan-a address 10.10.1.10 via static-host-mapping and DNS forwarding, and node2 (OPNsense) resolves app.internal to node4's lan-b address 10.10.2.10 via an unbound host override, each verified by resolution tests from the respective LAN host both before and after a full restart cycle. The mandatory node-restart evidence protocol was completed and independently corroborated by the fixed lifecycle boot-identity snapshots for all four nodes. Operational hygiene is good: temporary probe addresses and diagnostic capture files were reverted or cleaned, with only a minor, low-risk leftover config backup file on node2 and an unresolved background dhclient timeout on node3 that did not appear to affect final state.
limitations: The trace does not show an explicit deletion of node1's /tmp/eth1.log and /tmp/eth2.log tcpdump output files; their absence in the after-executor snapshot is attributable to the subsequent reboot rather than an explicit cleanup command.

The backup files config.xml.bak-iface and config.xml.bak-fwdns on node2 were referenced as existing but never explicitly deleted or inspected for content; their exact size/impact could not be verified from the captured evidence.

The outcome of the node3 background 'sudo dhclient -v ens7' command (cmd-97f165e8d7354fed) could not be confirmed because the proxy timed out before returning a result; whether it left a lingering dhclient process is indeterminate, though later commands show node3 converged on the intended static configuration.

operational_hygiene.summary: Diagnostic mutations were bounded and largely reverted or self-cleared. node1 had temporary link-local addresses (169.254.99.1/30 on eth1, 169.254.98.1/30 on eth2) added for topology probing (cmd-61e6d702a4134812) and explicitly removed afterward (cmd-8257b7828fc541e3). node3 and node4 similarly got temporary link-local probe addresses on ens7 (cmd-16ea0a63dfcb4437, cmd-2a6a96f8fddc47e5) that were superseded by a flush+static-assign to the final address (cmd-2dddf586d00a4e5d, cmd-549243929492436b), leaving no residual link-local addressing. Diagnostic tcpdump capture files on node2 (/tmp/*.pcap) and helper python scripts (/tmp/opnsense_iface.py, /tmp/opnsense_fw_dns.py) were explicitly removed at cmd-86028ea8b40b4c51. node1's own tcpdump log files (/tmp/eth1.log, /tmp/eth2.log, written at cmd-90aa23134b9b474e) were not explicitly deleted, but node1 was rebooted afterward, which clears /tmp (confirmed by global:after_executor:node1:temporary-files showing no such files present). One minor unresolved item: node2 retains config.xml.bak-iface and config.xml.bak-fwdns backup files (referenced at cmd-86028ea8b40b4c51) that were never removed; these are low-risk pre-change backups rather than harmful residue. A background dhclient probe on node3 (cmd-97f165e8d7354fed) timed out at the proxy layer with unclear resulting state, but subsequent commands show node3 ending on the intended static configuration, so no lasting negative effect is evident. No failed or conflicting services, no package-manager damage, and no weakened security controls were observed in the final state.
